questions.q: What does "fungible" actually mean, as defined in this lesson?
options: Every unit is identical and interchangeable, like dollars or Bitcoin
The token has no real value
The token can never be transferred
Each token is unique and non-interchangeable
questions.explain: Fungible means each token is exactly the same as every other token of the same type — the defining property ERC-20 tokens must have.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what is ERC-20 actually?
options: A separate blockchain from Ethereum
A type of Ethereum wallet
A smart contract written in Solidity that tracks who owns how many tokens and lets people transfer them
A physical coin or object
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit: ERC-20 is not a coin — it's a smart contract standard that keeps track of ownership and enables transfers.

questions.q: What does the `allowance` function actually check?
options: The total supply of the token
Whether a transfer has already happened
The token's name and symbol
How much a spender is still allowed to spend on behalf of a given owner
questions.explain: allowance(owner, spender) reports the remaining amount a spender is approved to move from a specific owner's balance.

questions.q: What does the real Transfer event fire in response to?
options: Only when a contract is first deployed
Only when the total supply changes
Only when the decimals value is set
Any time tokens actually move between addresses
questions.explain: The Transfer event logs every real movement of tokens from one address to another, whether via transfer, transferFrom, minting, or burning.

questions.q: What does the real `decimals` state variable actually control?
options: The token's total supply cap
How many addresses can hold the token
Whether the token can be transferred at all
How divisible the token is — most real tokens use 18, similar to how a dollar divides into 100 cents
questions.explain: decimals determines how many fractional places the token supports — 18 is the real, common standard most ERC-20 tokens use.
